title: Airbnb unlikely to let AI agents like Muse make bookings, CEO says
source_used: Nikkei Asia (opening paragraph only; rest paywalled)
key_facts: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said the platform is unlikely to let outside AI agents such as Meta's Muse book accommodation for users.
Nikkei frames this as part of growing concern among travel companies that AI assistants could weaken their direct relationship with customers.
Chesky argued that 'planning travel is entertainment', according to Nikkei's sub-headline.
The remarks come from a recent interview; Nikkei's dateline is Palo Alto, California.
AI agents here means software designed to browse websites and complete transactions on a user's behalf.
quote_evidence: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said the vacation rental platform is unlikely to allow such outside artificial intelligence agents as Meta Platforms' Muse to book accommodations for users, reflecting growing concerns among travel companies that AI assistants could weaken direct engagement with consumers.
'Planning travel is entertainment,' Brian Chesky argues as firm seeks to avoid being bypassed
why_it_matters_hint: A major consumer platform is drawing a line against being reduced to a back end for other companies' AI agents.
notes: Only the sub-headline, photo caption and first paragraph were readable; the body is behind Nikkei's paywall. No other outlet carried the story in Google News within 4 days. Facts limited to the lede.
